subject: Transportation Systems
title: Autonomous Trucks on Highways
description: A micro-lesson that makes Autonomous Trucks on Highways usable.

hook.text: Highway trucking may go autonomous before city driving. Highways are simpler—no pedestrians, predictable lanes.

buildup.text: Companies like Aurora aim for 'transfer hub' models: autonomous on highways, human drivers for city miles.

discovery.text: A self-driving truck running 24 hours would double the daily distance of a human-driven truck.

twist.text: 3.5 million US truck drivers could face job displacement. The transition raises massive labor questions.

climax.text: Autonomous highway trucking could cut shipping costs by 30%. The economic incentive is enormous.

punchline.text: The easiest part of driving to automate may transform an entire industry.

quiz.question: Why is highway trucking easier to automate than city driving?
options: Highways have predictable lanes, few pedestrians, and controlled access
